questions.q: What should run automatically on every pull request that changes Terraform code?
options: terraform plan, so the computed diff is visible in the PR before merge
terraform apply, so the change takes effect immediately
terraform destroy, to reset the environment for testing
Nothing — Terraform changes should never run in CI/CD
questions.explain: Plan on every PR mirrors Git/GitHub/CI-CD Lesson 19's pattern of running tests automatically on every commit — but for infrastructure.

questions.q: Why shouldn't terraform apply run automatically the instant a PR merges to main, with no further gate?
options: Because a human should still approve the apply step before real infrastructure is actually created, changed, or destroyed
Because terraform apply cannot run inside GitHub Actions at all
Because merging a PR never triggers any CI workflow
Because apply always fails when run from CI/CD
questions.explain: A required approval gate (a GitHub environment with reviewers) adds the same human-in-the-loop discipline Lesson 20's real workflow modeled for application deploys.

questions.q: Where should Azure credentials (client ID, secret, tenant ID, subscription ID) live for a Terraform CI/CD workflow?
options: As CI secrets, injected as environment variables at run time — never in a .tf file or a commit
Hardcoded directly in the .tf file for convenience
In a comment at the top of the workflow YAML
In the pull request description
questions.explain: Git/GitHub/CI-CD Lesson 23 covered exactly this: secrets belong in the CI platform's secret store, not in code.

questions.q: What specific value does running terraform plan on every PR add, even though a human still approves the apply?
options: It surfaces the actual computed diff for review before anyone decides whether to approve the apply
It replaces the need for any human review entirely
It automatically fixes any mistakes in the .tf files
It has no value if apply is still gated by approval
questions.explain: The approval decision is only as good as the information behind it — the plan output is exactly what a reviewer needs to see before approving.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what comes right after Chapter 4 (IaC in Practice)?
options: Chapter 5, this course's capstone, provisioning a real data platform's infrastructure
A new course entirely unrelated to Terraform or Bicep
A repeat of Chapter 1's fundamentals
Nothing — Chapter 4 is the end of the course
questions.explain: Chapter 4 closes out IaC-in-practice topics; Chapter 5 is the course's final chapter, its capstone.
